description: The skill sidecar contract, as cases. Postmortem item C1 (docs/postmortems/2026-09-22-chains-halt-invalid-block-shape.md): MEASURED 2026-09-22 on the operator's host, a skill wrote its audit trail INSIDE the chain corpus (`chains/halt/*.json`), and a non-conforming block there crashed Memphis at the next boot. The rule existed only as a paragraph in the postmortem. The original wording asked for a `compat.test.sh` per skill — that is a copy of one rule in every skill directory, and a copy per directory is how rules drift. So the rule has ONE owner (`src/infra/audit/skill-sidecar-contract.ts`), every skill DECLARES where it writes, and two runners read it: the gate (`scripts/check-skill-contracts.mts`) and this corpus. {skill} = the SKILL.md text under test; {expectedRules} = the rules that must fire, in order.

cases.name: a skill that says nothing about its writes cannot be checked
a contract that omits the audit target is incomplete
a contract that omits the sidecar writes is incomplete
an empty declaration is not an answer
a sidecar write under chains/ is the shape that crashed the runtime
a relative chains/ path is under the corpus too
